clue.text: Embarrassed firm coming before the magistrate

parts.note: firm means hard, solid to the touch
someone up before the magistrate is appearing in court, so the phrase gives UP

explanation.surface: Someone is mortified because their company has been hauled into the magistrates' court.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short of money leaves one financially embarrassed, the old polite phrase for poverty.

clue.text: Piece of banana the main course? What a hateful thing!

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A diner recoils at being served a chunk of banana as the main dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'course?' into the definition; it belongs to the hidden-word stretch 'banana the main course', leaving 'What a hateful thing' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one loathes utterly is an object of detestation, a curse in the original church sense.

clue.text: Draw figure and render an account

explanation.surface: An artist sketches a shape and then writes up a report on it.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry one traces a circle or other shape this way; equally it means to narrate or give a verbal picture of something.

clue.text: Casting director in the theatre?

parts.note: not the person who picks actors but a tradesman who makes moulded casts and decorative mouldings for a theatre's walls and ceilings

explanation.surface: A question about the person who chooses actors for a stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who works with gypsum makes cast cornices and mouldings, so he directs the casting of ornament in a playhouse.

clue.text: Writer whose creations are snuffed out

explanation.surface: A novelist whose works are suppressed or killed off.
explanation.walkthrough: Raymond Chandler was the American crime novelist; a chandler is also a candle-maker, whose products are snuffed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler wrote hard-boiled detective novels; a candle-maker's wax lights are what get extinguished.

clue.text: For an abundance, divide the cards and make new effort

parts.note: to cut is to split the pack before dealing
to come again is to return for another attempt

explanation.surface: A card game where plenty is had by cutting the pack and trying once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut-and-come-again' describes a plentiful supply, like a joint one can keep slicing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes plenty, a supply one can keep helping oneself from without exhausting it.

clue.text: The ne plus ultra fashionable sort of gear

indicators.note: fashionable here means fashioned, shaped anew, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Praise for the very latest, most stylish kind of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' rearranges NE and ULTRA; 'plus' merely joins them, and 'gear' means a car's gear, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The position of a gearbox in which no gear is engaged is a kind of gear setting.

clue.text: Ground-rent deposit, Conservative concludes, is a convenience

indicators.note: concludes says the Conservative piece comes at the end

parts.note: molten rock deposited from a rent or fissure in the ground is lava
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A landlord's ground-rent deposit is settled by a Tory, which is handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground-rent' looks like a property charge; read it as a rent (split) in the ground, from which lava flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A public convenience is the British euphemism for a toilet.

clue.text: Revolutionary movement considered a result of Doppler effect

parts.note: red is the colour of revolutionaries and communists
a shift is a movement or change of position

explanation.surface: A political uprising is judged to be a product of a physics phenomenon.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from receding galaxies is stretched to longer wavelengths, a consequence of the Doppler effect.

clue.text: One found under a bonnet with a rod on the river

indicators.note: on puts the rod piece after the river piece

parts.note: the Cam is the river at Cambridge
a shaft is a rod or pole

explanation.surface: A woman in a bonnet fishing with a rod beside the river.
explanation.walkthrough: A bonnet is the British word for a car's hood, not a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating engine part sits beneath the hood of a car.

clue.text: Smoked about five and went round the bend

indicators.note: about means the word for smoked goes around the numeral

parts.note: smoked fish or meat is cured
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Someone smoked about five cigarettes and then went mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A road that bent round a corner followed a bend; the phrase here is literal, not madness.

clue.text: Cabinet-maker adapting another's design

indicators.note: adapting signals that the letters of the word are reworked into a new order

parts.note: the word is used letter for letter, its S included

explanation.surface: A furniture maker copies a rival's pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' completes the surface; Thomas Sheraton was an 18th-century English furniture designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton was a celebrated English furniture designer of the Georgian era.

clue.text: It props up the sign of an old friar

definitions.text: the sign of an old friar

explanation.surface: Something holding up a medieval friar's emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crutched Friars were a medieval order whose badge was a cross, called a crutch.
explanation.definitionFit: A support for the lame holds a person up; the Crutched Friars took their name from the cross they wore as an emblem.

clue.text: Maker of counterfeit notes, as from genuine bills

definitions.text: Maker of counterfeit notes, as from genuine bills

parts.words: Maker of counterfeit notes, as from genuine bills
parts.note: not a forger of banknotes but a device imitating the song notes that come from real beaks

explanation.surface: A forger turns out fake money that looks like real banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter's whistle imitates the song of real birds, so its notes are fakes of those from beaks.

clue.text: The very album for the autumn!

definitions.text: The very album for the autumn!

parts.words: The very album for the autumn!
parts.note: an album whose pages come out, fitting a season when foliage drops off the trees

explanation.surface: Recommending the perfect scrapbook or photo album for autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A binder with removable pages suits autumn, when foliage comes away from the branches.

clue.text: Husband to take care of?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a husband exists to look after things.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband resources is to conserve them; to keep something safe is to look after it.

clue.text: Toledo housing

parts.note: not homes in the Spanish city but a sheath for a Toledo blade, the city famous for its swords

explanation.surface: Residential property in the Spanish city of Toledo.
explanation.definitionFit: A Toledo is a fine sword, and a sheath houses a sword.

clue.text: Octavian is desperate for a break

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild disorder, so the letters of the Roman name are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The Roman emperor-to-be badly needs a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday is a break from work or study.

clue.text: Island boat-crew, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for the crew is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: The crew of a boat from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: An eyot (or ait) is a small island in a river, such as on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot is a small river islet.

clue.text: Having a part taken for granted, like the Oval

definitions.text: Having a part taken for granted

explanation.surface: Describing something assumed, like a famous cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground; an oval is an elliptical shape. Ellipsis leaves words understood.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellipsis omits words the reader supplies; an oval has the shape of an ellipse.

clue.text: Dare I nod off, being appointed to the ministry?

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or awry, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drowsy candidate wonders whether he may doze during his ordination.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest made so by a bishop has been admitted to holy orders, appointed as a minister.

clue.text: Haydn symphony for the Edinburgh tattoo?

explanation.surface: Choosing a Haydn work to play at the military tattoo in Edinburgh.
explanation.walkthrough: Haydn's Symphony No 103 is nicknamed the Drumroll; a tattoo is also a drumbeat, and the Edinburgh Military Tattoo is a famous display.
explanation.definitionFit: Haydn's 103rd symphony opens with a timpani flourish; a tattoo is a rapid beat on a drum.

clue.text: The Camptown leaflet to take away

parts.note: the song Camptown Races begins De Camptown ladies, using the dialect form of the
a tract is a pamphlet or leaflet

explanation.surface: A leaflet about Camptown is being removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camptown Races' is a Stephen Foster minstrel song whose words open 'De Camptown ladies sing dis song'.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract from something is to diminish or subtract from it.

clue.text: Sylvia's concomitant of kindness

parts.note: in Shakespeare's song Who is Silvia? a quality is said to live with kindness, and the clue asks for it

explanation.surface: Sylvia's companion trait is kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: From the song in The Two Gentlemen of Verona: 'Is she kind as she is fair? For beauty lives with kindness.'
explanation.definitionFit: The song says loveliness dwells with kindness, so attractiveness is kindness's companion.

clue.text: Confused, man embracing Heather could be a Unionist, for example

indicators.note: embracing means the jumbled man goes round the heather word
confused means the letters of man are mixed up

parts.note: erica is the botanical name for heather

explanation.surface: A bewildered man hugging a woman called Heather might be a political unionist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant's botanical name. In the American Civil War, Northern supporters of the Union were called Unionists.
explanation.definitionFit: A Northern supporter of the Union in the US Civil War was a citizen of the United States.

clue.text: Horse, for example, making come-back for the plate

indicators.note: making a come-back means the word for plate is read backwards

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer

explanation.surface: A racehorse makes a return for a trophy plate race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plate' suggests a horse race prize; it means a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse is one example of a creature, a member of the beast kingdom.

clue.text: A part of Rome's foundation has an air-hole in one quarter

parts.note: an gives the single letter A
a vent is an opening to let air through
E for east, one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: A Roman building's foundations include an air-vent in one district.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aventine is one of the seven hills on which Rome was founded; 'quarter' means a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aventine is one of Rome's seven hills, on which the city was built.

clue.text: Fellow at No 10 with name for largess

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a college
the number 10 is written with the figures one and nought, read as I and O

explanation.surface: A man at Downing Street hands out generous gifts in his own name.
explanation.walkthrough: No 10 Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's residence; here the digits 1 and 0 become letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Largess is generous giving, and a gift is such a giving.

clue.text: Walton's bunch of keys for the front

explanation.surface: A set of keys belonging to Walton is at the front door.
explanation.walkthrough: Façade is William Walton's entertainment to Edith Sitwell's poems; F, A, C, A, D, E are all musical keys.
explanation.definitionFit: Walton composed Façade; its letters are all note names; and a building's face is its frontage.
